To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology of HDPESEBS blends can be controlled to improve the thermal stability of PE.
the morphology of the HDPESEBS blend can affect the thermal stability and the dielectric properties.
the morphology of the blend has been tailored to control the dielectric properties and the AC breakdown strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new polymeric materials for high voltage insulation applications, based on the combination of High Density Polyethylene HDPE with the Styrene-Ethene-Butene-Styrene SEBStriblock copolymer.

the study of a polymer blend with a tailored morphology, which is able to improve the thermal stability of the HDPE matrix and, at the same time, to maintain the dielectric properties of the polymer blend at the same level as that of the HDPE.
the study of the dielectric response of a HDPE/SEBS blend in which the morphology has been controlled by varying the composition and the processing conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the morphology of the blend has a significant effect on its dielectric properties and the AC breakdown strength, while the thermal stability remains unchanged.

, in the case of the HDPESEBS blend, the droplet-like morphology is the best configuration for the improvement of the thermal and dielectric stability of the polymer blend, while the fiber-like morphology should be avoided.
the SEBS/HDPE blend with fiber-like morphology exhibits an improved thermal stability, a decreased dielectric loss and a decreased AC breakdown strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of SEBS in the HDPE matrix induces the formation of a blend morphology that is strongly dependent on the SEBS concentration in the polymer mixture.
the morphology of the blend has to be taken into account when evaluating its thermal stability and dielectric response.
the morphology plays a key role in the dielectric properties of the blend.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of a blend can be tailored to improve the thermal stability of one of the components, without affecting significantly the dielectric properties of the blend.
the dielectric properties of the HDPE/SEBS blend are highly dependent on the blend morphology.
the morphology of polymer blends plays a key role in determining the dielectric properties and the AC breakdown strength.
